title: Mbappé, Haaland, and Messi Lead 2026 FIFA World Cup Dream XI
excerpt: FIFA's fan-voted team of the tournament features Golden Boot winner Mbappé, surprise selection Vozinha, and breakout stars from the historic 48-team competition across North America.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Mbappé scored 10 goals, winning the Golden Boot and reaching 22 World Cup goals in 22 matches.
  • Vozinha, a 40-year-old goalkeeper, topped fan votes despite Unai Simón winning the Golden Glove.
  • Spain had three players in the Dream XI, reflecting their triumph over Argentina in the final.
  • Haaland scored seven goals, including a brace that eliminated Brazil in the Round of 16.

FIFA has unveiled the fan-voted Dream Team of the 2026 World Cup, with Golden Boot winner Kylian Mbappé, England's Jude Bellingham, and Spain's Marc Cucurella headlining an XI that blends tournament champions with breakout performers from the historic 48-team competition held across North America.

Vozinha: The People's Goalkeeper

The most striking selection was in goal, where Cape Verde's Vozinha — a 40-year-old who was without a club after leaving Portuguese second-tier side Chaves before the tournament — topped the goalkeeper vote with 39.6 percent. His inclusion came despite Spain's Unai Simón winning the Golden Glove, the award selected by FIFA's technical study group.

Vozinha's case was built on a series of extraordinary performances for the World Cup debutants. He made seven saves as Cape Verde held eventual champions Spain to a goalless draw and later helped take Argentina to extra time in the Round of 32, displays that captured the imagination of fans worldwide.

![Jude Bellingham. Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/2/23/Jude_Bellingham_England_v_Ghana_23_June_2026-061_%28cropped%29.jpg)

Spain's Defensive Wall and Rodri's Midfield Mastery

Champions Spain contributed the largest contingent to the Dream XI. Full-backs Pedro Porro and Cucurella earned their places through relentless overlapping runs and disciplined defensive coverage that locked down the flanks throughout the tournament. Alongside them, France's Dayot Upamecano and Argentina's Lisandro Martínez completed a formidable back four.

"Rodri dictated the tempo of every match for Spain, leading all players with a staggering 94.5 completed passes per game."

— World Soccer Talk

In midfield, Golden Ball winner Rodri anchored the Dream XI alongside Bellingham, who directly contributed to seven goals as England achieved their best performance on foreign soil with a third-place finish. France's Michael Olise, in his World Cup debut, completed the trio after recording seven assists — breaking Pelé's 56-year-old single-tournament assist record set during the 1970 World Cup in Mexico.

A Forward Line for the Ages

The attacking trident of Lionel Messi, Erling Haaland, and Mbappé represents three generations of footballing greatness. Messi, at 39, delivered another heroic campaign with eight goals and four assists, directly factoring into 12 of Argentina's 19 goals as the Albiceleste reached the final before falling to Spain.

Club Status Before Tournament

Haaland, leading Norway to their first World Cup appearance in 28 years, announced himself on the global stage with seven goals in five matches. His iconic brace eliminated five-time champions Brazil 2-1 in the Round of 16 before Norway's run ended against England in the quarterfinals.

Mbappé, meanwhile, cemented his status among football's all-time greats. The 27-year-old French forward's 10-goal haul brought his career tally to 22 World Cup goals in 22 matches, a ratio unmatched in the modern era.

What It Means for the Diaspora

The tournament's expanded 48-team format saw increased representation from across the globe, with debutants Cape Verde's run resonating strongly with diaspora communities worldwide. India did not qualify, but the spectacle of the first World Cup in North America since 1994 drew millions of Indian-American fans to stadiums in the United States, Canada, and Mexico.

Looking Ahead

With the 2030 World Cup set to be hosted across Spain, Portugal, and Morocco — with centenary matches in Uruguay, Argentina, and Paraguay — the players celebrated in this Dream XI will look to extend their legacies on yet another global stage.
